title: Handover document frontmatter
description: Contract for the YAML frontmatter of every .context/handovers/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md document, read by validate-handover.sh. A handover is a point-in-time snapshot written by an outgoing session so another agent/session can resume the work without re-deriving context.

title.description: Short, specific description of the work handed over, e.g. "TICKET-123 example-service dev rollout - mid-migration".

type.description: Fixed discriminator so handovers are distinguishable from other .context/ typologies (findings, plans, follow-ups).

date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the handover was written. Must match the date segment in the filename.

branch.description: Git branch (or worktree branch) the outgoing session was working on, e.g. feat/ticket-123-example-service-dev.

status.description: active: not yet picked up. done: a session picked this up and closed out the outstanding work (flip in the same change that resolves it, never delete the file). superseded: replaced by a newer handover on the same branch/topic.

session_id.description: Optional. The outgoing session/worktree identifier (e.g. matching a .context/logs/<session_id>/ directory), so a follow-up session can trace back to the original transcript if needed.

author.description: Optional. Who or what wrote the handover (a person's name/email, or an agent identifier).

tags.description: Optional free-text tags for search, following the same convention as .context/follow-ups/ frontmatter.

related.description: Optional. Repo-relative paths to related plans, follow-ups, tickets, or PRs/MRs this handover concerns.

supersedes.description: Optional. Repo-relative path to an earlier handover this one replaces, when a topic gets more than one handover over time.

x-date-invariant: The filename's YYYY-MM-DD segment must equal the frontmatter 'date' field.
x-filename-rule: The file this frontmatter lives in must be named YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md under .context/handovers/, matching this repo's follow-up/plan naming convention.
x-lifecycle-rule: status starts 'active'. The session that picks up the outstanding work flips it to 'done' in the same change that resolves it - never delete the file, per this repo's follow-up lifecycle convention.
